source: Quiz 5 - Sessions 1-6: Model Training, Alignment, and the Agent Harness
question: Why can a model produce different responses to different inputs while its learned weights remain fixed?

options.text: Its weights and intermediate representations refer to the same numbers
options.feedback: The notes distinguish learned weights from the representations produced during processing. Confusing them makes an ordinary inference change look like training.

options.text: The new input acts as a human preference comparison during training
options.feedback: Receiving input is not the same as training on human comparisons. An ordinary response can change through input-dependent processing without a learning update.

options.text: Its intermediate representations depend on the input being processed
options.feedback: Inference uses existing weights while processing the current input. Changing representations are different from changes to the weights themselves.

options.text: Each new input supplies an error signal that updates learned parameters
options.feedback: This confuses ordinary input-dependent processing with training. Training uses a learning process to update parameters; a new input alone does not establish such an update.
